**Summary:**

New figures from outsourcing data company Tussell reveal that UK public bodies paid private consultants £3.4bn last year, a 62% (£1.3bn) increase compared to 2019-20. Spending on consultants surged during the Covid pandemic and has not returned to pre-pandemic levels.

This poses a significant challenge for Keir Starmer's government, which has pledged to halve consultant spending during this parliament. However, nearly £650m in new consultancy contracts have been awarded since Labour took power, though many were agreed before the transition. Notably, KPMG secured a contract worth up to £223m to train civil servants starting in August — the second-largest public sector contract ever awarded to the firm.

Labour peer and accounting academic Prem Sikka criticised the trend as "scandalous," arguing that consultants contribute little of real value, as they cannot meaningfully understand complex organisations in just a few weeks.
